title: Gear ratios
body: When two gears mesh, their teeth pass each other at the same rate. So a gear with more teeth turns more slowly than a gear with fewer teeth, and the two turn in opposite directions.
The gear ratio is the output gear's teeth divided by the motor gear's teeth. A 12-tooth motor gear driving a 36-tooth output gear has a ratio of 3, so the output turns 3 times slower.
You don't get something for nothing. Slowing the output down multiplies its turning force (torque) by about the same ratio; friction takes a little. That's how a small motor can lift a heavy load.
equation: output speed = motor speed × motor teeth ÷ output teeth
realWorld: Bikes use the same trade. A low gear makes hills easier to climb, but you pedal faster for the same road speed.
sources: Lynch, K. M. & Park, F. C. (2017). Modern Robotics, §8.9 Actuation, Gearing and Friction. https://modernrobotics.northwestern.edu/nu-gm-book-resource/8-9-actuation-gearing-and-friction
Lehrer, R. & Schauble, L. (1998). Reasoning about structure and function: Children's conceptions of gears. Journal of Research in Science Teaching 35(1), 3–25.
